title: Fugaro run record (result.json)
description: The run record the runner writes to runs/<repo-slug>/<run-id>/result.json (design §4.6).

execution.description: The canonical full execution name; empty or absent for local runs.

stage.description: The step the run is in. plan and render are a mode: artifact run's optional plan stage and its render step (design artifact-runs.md §3).

outcome.description: Empty while the run is in progress. artifacts is a mode: artifact run whose deliverable is in the runs bucket: it opens no pull request.

base_branch.description: The base the run's pull request targets: git.base_branch of the config it ran with. A follow-up takes it as its ref.

start_sha.description: The commit the run's branch was cut from (the task's ref as bootstrap read it), which is the base every question of what this run changed is measured against. A follow-up records it as follow_up.start_sha instead; a mode: review run has no branch.

desc.description: Digest of the title and description the runner last wrote, outside the status section.

status_at.description: When the runner last wrote the status section into the description; a running record with an old value is the stale draft of a run that died.

draft_fallback.description: The host refused draft pull requests; the PR is a normal one with a [DRAFT] title prefix.

tier.description: first: the coder model's first-line review, never decides readiness; senior: the reviewer's; adversarial: level 3's, which reviews after the senior's, so its rejection bounces the run into the cheap loop and this level is not reviewed again (docs/review-levels-ab-jobmax D727). Absent in a run without a first line (senior).

head.description: The commit this review read. A level approves one head, and the levels' heads can differ within a round: a level reviewed again after a fix has the later one, and a level the bounce skipped keeps the earlier one. Absent when the round recorded none, which is every record written before this field existed.

bounce.description: Which cheap loop this review followed, under review: {bounce: first_line} (docs/recipes.md section 1, internal/runstore's ReviewSummary.Bounce). Absent (0) for a review before any senior rejection and on every senior review, 1 for the first-line loop after the first senior rejection, 2 after the second, and so on. The catalog recipes `standard` and `test-and-fix` set the bounce, so a schema missing this field refuses the record of their own bounced runs.

cost_usd.description: The model spend, summed over stages.

compute_usd.description: Meaningful only when compute_estimated is true; otherwise 0.

compute_estimated.description: True only when the backend's prices and the workflow's resources were known.

compute_source.description: The price table compute_usd was priced from, in the table's own words, so a reader can tell an estimate priced from the Compute Engine VM table from one priced with Cloud Run's jobs list price. Absent for Cloud Run's list price (and for every record written before the field existed), which is why it is not required.

total_usd.description: Billed dollars only: excludes the model figure when model_basis is subscription.

model_notional_usd.description: The part of model_usd that was notional: what the calls a subscription paid for would have cost at list rates (an oauth run's every call, and a cascade run's tier A, D140). It is never in total_usd. model_usd keeps its meaning -- every stage's model dollars, notional ones included -- so sum(stages[].model_usd) + model_by["unattributed"] == model_usd still holds exactly, and this says how much of it was notional. A mixed run's model_basis is api-list for the whole run, so a reader splitting the run's dollars must split on this field, never on model_basis. Absent when nothing was notional, and in records written before this field existed.

model_source.description: Where model_usd came from: the gateway's settled ledger or Claude Code's own total.

model_by.description: Model spend in USD, by model.

route_by.description: Model spend in USD, by provider route; calls on Anthropic have no route.

reported_usd.description: What providers said their calls cost, summed. For comparison with model_usd: it never prices a call the table priced, but it floors the charge for a service tier no one prices (up to that call's reservation), so a model_usd above it is not always an overcharge.

unreconciled.description: USD charged from reservations rather than from reported usage.

cache_read_tokens.description: The run's prompt-cache read token total, summed from the gateway's per-call usage. A token count and not a dollar split: the price table returns one blended figure per call, so a cache read's dollars cannot be told from a write's (P12). Absent when the run read nothing from cache, and for a run with no gateway.

cache_write_tokens.description: The run's prompt-cache write token total, summed from the gateway's per-call usage, both cache TTLs together. Absent when the run wrote nothing to cache, and for a run with no gateway.

usage_unparsed.description: Calls settled at their reservation because their usage could not be read.

service_tiers.description: The service tiers the run's calls came back at that the price table has no multiplier for, spelled as a violation is (`usage.service_tier "priority"`). Those calls were charged the conservative multiple of the rates each call was priced at -- or, where the route reported what the call cost, the dearer of that multiple and the provider's own figure plus the route fee, up to the reservation that call made -- rather than failing their stage, so model_usd counts that charge and this is what names it. At most eight distinct names, then one `+N more` entry counting the distinct names beyond them, so a provider that answers a new tier on every call cannot grow the record with the call count. Absent when every call was priced at the model's own rates.

catalog_stale.description: True when the built-in provider price catalog was older than its own 30-day threshold (catalog.StaleAfter, internal/pricing/catalog), so every model it priced was charged the dearest end of its tier's range rather than the end price_policy asked for. The run over-counts on purpose and logs one `budget: price catalog stale` WARN. Absent when the catalog was fresh, or when no catalog-priced model was charged.

calls.description: How many model calls the stage made: the gateway's stage report. Absent without a gateway, so on an oauth run, where no result event supplies a call count either, and absent when nobody counted -- which is not the same as a stage that made no calls (0).

agents.description: How many sub-agent tool calls the stage's own stream carried, counted by the relay for every auth mode, gateway or not. The gateway's count of distinct agent IDs is a different figure and is never recorded, because it rests on the agent ID a client claims. Absent when nobody counted, which is not the same as a stage that ran none (0).

repeats.description: The most times one identical shell command ran in the stage, counted by the relay from the stage's own stream. A count alone, never the command, a hash of it or any argument: a command can carry a token or a path, and this record is read by every launcher and by the digest's report, which flags a stage at five repeats or more as a loop (task-governance T1.4, D332). Absent when nobody counted, and in records written before the field existed, which is not the same as a stage that ran no command (0).

model_usd.description: What this stage's model calls cost, whatever model they were on: the gateway's figure for the stage (the background model's calls included), or, without the gateway, the result event's total_cost_usd. The stages sum to cost.model_usd to the micro-dollar, except for gateway spend that settled after its stage's wait ran out, which is cost.model_by's "unattributed" and in no stage.

model.description: The model the stage was pinned to: the stage role's models.<role>, else agent.model. It is not what the upstream served, and a stage may also have called the background model, so it does not account for model_usd on its own. Absent when the config pinned none.

model_notional_usd.description: The part of this stage's model_usd that was notional: Claude Code's own figure when the stage ran on oauth, and, in a cascade run, the tier-A calls' share of what the gateway settled (D140). The stage's own split is the only place it exists -- one stage of a cascade run can hold both -- so cost.model_notional_usd says how much of the run's figure was notional and this says where. Absent when the stage's figure was all billed.

switches.description: The run's switch log (D140): every credential switch the credentials service reported on one of this run's calls, in the order the gateway settled the answers that carried them. Names and reason words of the service's contract, never a credential value, and nothing reads it to decide anything. Absent for a run that never switched, and in records written before this field existed.

from.description: The credential the call was on; absent when the call started on the credential that answered it (the service's own meaning for an empty from).

reason.description: Why the cascade moved, one of the credentials service's closed set of reason words (credsvc.ValidReason), never free text.

cache_miss_usd.description: The estimated cost of re-reading what the previous call had cached, priced at the answering tier's input rate less its cache-read rate (F24). An estimate for a reader, charged to nothing: the ledger settles the calls themselves.

cache_miss_unmeasured.description: True when the answering tier's cache behaviour is not measured (a Claude model on tier C's OpenRouter route, F24, Checks 46 and 50). Then the miss is unknown rather than free, and cache_miss_usd is 0 because there is no figure, not because it is one.

image.description: What the image the run started in was built from, read before the checkout was synced.

built_at.description: When the image was built; absent when the image doesn't say.

baked_commit.description: The baked checkout's HEAD when the run started.

follow_up.description: Set for a run that continues an existing pull request (design §4.4).

start_sha.description: The pull request's head the run started from.

comments.description: How many comments reached the agent.

authors.description: Display name to the number of that author's comments used.

untrusted_authors.description: Display names whose comments were dropped as untrusted, sorted.

untrusted_author_count.description: How many distinct untrusted authors were dropped, those beyond the 20 named included.

halt.description: Why the run was halted; set when status is halted.

checkpoint.description: The report a governance halt leaves (docs/task-governance/implementation-plan.md T6.1, D329, G7): why the run stopped, and what a person deciding whether to continue it needs to know. A governance stop is never a silent kill — it halts the run and opens a draft pull request carrying this report — so the block is written exactly where halt.reason is one of the governance reasons, and no other stop (a cap, a kill switch, a failure) writes one. trigger, why_over and estimate_usd are the runner's own values read from the record; done, next and hard_instructions are the stopping agent's answer to the checkpoint prompt (wired in T7.3), so they are absent for every checkpoint written before that stage exists and for a per-run cap or stage timeout, which gets no checkpoint call. Every text field is bounded at runstore.MaxCheckpointText runes. Absent — never an empty block — for a run that did not take a governance halt, and in records from before this field existed; the field is additive, so an old reader sees the record it always saw and `version` stays 1.

trigger.description: Which tripwire stopped the run (internal/runstore's governance HaltReason constants): a stage past its own budget, review that spent more calls than the ratio allows, more distinct sub-agents than the maximum, a review range covering files the run's own commits never changed, or a run past the cost its tier expected. The runner sets it from those constants, never from task text, so a reader renders the value itself.

done.description: What the work had finished when the run stopped, in the stopping agent's own words, clipped to 500 runes (runstore.MaxCheckpointText). Model-written: a reader treats it as untrusted text, never as markup.

why_over.description: Why the run is over, in the runner's own words for the trigger it recorded (internal/runner's haltReasonText), so the report says what the tripwire was without repeating the halt's own detail.

next.description: What the work would do next to finish the task, in the stopping agent's own words, bounded the same way.

estimate_usd.description: The money the work had cost when it stopped, as the record's cost_usd holds it: the runner's only money figure for a checkpoint, and the figure a continuation starts from. Notional dollars included, the way cost_usd includes them.

hard_instructions.description: What the work found hard to satisfy or contradictory in its instructions, if anything, in the stopping agent's own words, bounded the same way.

policy.description: The budget and model policy the run ran under, merged from the project's published policy, the owner's ceiling, the default branch's fugaro.yaml and the run's own. Absent when no layer set any.

per_day_usd.description: The committed daily cap of the repository (fugaro.yaml); the run enforces it client-side against the repository's day counter.

allowed_models.description: Present means a restriction: an empty list forbids every model. Absent means every model is allowed.

sources.description: Policy key to the layer that set its effective value: ceiling, policy (the project's published node, which replaces the ceiling key by key), default-branch or branch.

ignored.description: Values a layer set that the run dropped: a value looser than the limits in force, or — absent clamped, below — a stage timeout the run's own timeouts.stage bounds at least as tightly (T7.6).

source.description: The layer of the effective value.

from.description: The layer that asked for the dropped value. The ceiling is here for one case: a stage timeout the run's own timeouts.stage bounds at least as tightly, which the run drops and records (T7.6) — the layer that wrote it can be the project layer's governance, which is the ceiling.

clamped.description: True for the one shape that is not 'looser than the limits in force': a stage timeout the run's own timeouts.stage bounds at least as tightly, which the run drops rather than give a deadline of its own (T7.6). Absent (false) for the merge's looser values, which is also a stage timeout dropped because a tighter layer capped it — the two cannot be told apart by key, source and from alone.

budget.description: The run's part in the project's shared budget; absent when the run did not use the budget backend.

day.description: The UTC day number (days since 1970-01-01) the run started on.

granted_micros.description: Everything the run's leases granted, in micro-dollars (0 for an oauth run).

released_micros.description: What the run gave back unused, in micro-dollars.

pushed_head.description: The commit the run pushed, set right after a successful push.

finalize_reserve_s.description: The workflow's timeouts.finalize_reserve at the task's ref, overrides applied, in seconds; cancel floors its grace with it.

reviewed.description: Set for a mode: review run (outcome reviewed): one entry per pull request it reviewed.

render.description: What a mode: artifact run's render step did (design artifact-runs.md §3, D8). Absent for every other run, and for an artifact run refused before its render step.

command.description: The commands.render string with the redactor applied: the record never holds a secret value.

command_sha256.description: The sha256 of the string the runner RAN, unredacted: the commands.render text as the runner read it from fugaro.yaml at the run's ref, which a reviewer can hash too. It is deliberately NOT the hash of command whenever the redactor fired.

tree.description: The tree the render ran in: the working checkout the plan stage also had (design D8).

inputs.description: The files the launcher attached to this run (fugaro run --attach, design artifact-runs.md §4 step 6): the task spec's own list, echoed once the runner downloaded and verified every one, so a reader sees exactly what the run was given. Absent for a run launched without an attachment.

name.description: The name it is stored and written under: runs/<slug>/<run>/inputs/<name> in the bucket, <checkout>/inputs/<name> in the run. A name of nothing but whitespace is no name (task.InputNameBlank, the same rule the task schema and the launcher apply).

sha256.description: The sha256 the launcher read while uploading; the runner verified the object it downloaded against it.

artifacts.description: The files a mode: artifact run uploaded, in name order (design artifact-runs.md §3, §8): one entry per object under this run's artifacts/ prefix. Absent — never an empty array — for every run that delivered none, including every record written before this field existed.

name.description: The object's key leaf, relative to artifacts/: the sanitiser's own output, never a path out of the prefix, with no .. element, no leading dot, no NUL and no newline.

bytes.description: The size of the bytes in the bucket, as the upload measured them.

sha256.description: The sha256 of the bytes in the bucket, hashed in the same pass that wrote them and checked against the staged copy's hash.

content_type.description: Recorded, never trusted (§8.1): from the name's extension or a sniff of the first bytes.

probe.description: What commands.probe said about this artifact (design artifact-runs.md §3, plan Task 5). Every artifact this runner uploads carries one: a recipe that asks for no probe — outputs.probe: none, or the default — records {ran: false, exit_code: -1} rather than leaving the key out, so 'no probe ran' is stated in the record instead of inferred from a field that is not there (plan Review Focus 6), and a probe that did run records ran: true with the exit code it exited or was killed on (negative when a signal killed it, -1 for the SIGKILL after its grace). Absent only in a record written before the probe step existed.

ran.description: False when the recipe asked for no probe: the runner started no process at all. The exit code beside it is then -1 and not 0, because a reader skimming an exit code must never read 'skipped' as 'passed'.

warning.description: Empty when the probe passed. Deliberately unwritten by this release: a probe that fails refuses the upload, so a record carries no artifact whose verdict could hold one (plan Task 5).

changed_files.description: The paths the run changed, as the run itself recorded them at finalize (console v2 design D27, F17). Paths only: no contents, no diff, no commit message, no line counts. Bounded, with the truncation recorded rather than hidden. Absent for a run that recorded none — one that died before finalize, or whose git read failed — and absent means 'no record of what this run changed', never 'it changed nothing'.

paths.description: The paths, sorted as git listed them, at most 200 of them (runstore.MaxChangedFiles). Never null: an empty array is a run that changed no path, which is a different fact from the field being absent.

total.description: How many paths the run really changed, so a truncated record still says how big the set it is part of was.

truncated.description: Set only when paths is shorter than total, which happens at 200 paths or 16 KiB of path (runstore.MaxChangedPathBytes), whichever comes first: the stored set is then not the whole set.

rigor.description: The mode the run resolved, the layer that decided it, the areas that matched and the moment of the run each was known at (docs/rigor-modes/implementation-plan.md T1.2, D22, D24, D25). The mode's configuration is read from the base branch (D25), so revision names where it came from. Absent for a run that resolved none — a record from before this field existed, or a run that died before bootstrap — and absent means 'no record of this run's rigor', never 'it resolved nothing'.

mode.description: The resolved mode (internal/rigor's vocabulary; pro is Fugaro's built-in default, D19).

from.description: The layer that decided the mode: an area rule the run's paths matched, the repository's rigor.default, the project layer's defaults.rigor.default, Fugaro's built-in default, or the run's own request, which may raise and never lower (D6): fugaro run --mode, or the mode a --pr follow-up keeps from its pull request, which it records as request with or without the flag (T5.2). It is never reached: that is the resolver's answer to a later moment asking again — hold what you already have (D22) — and the record keeps the earlier, narrower reason instead, which is the layer that actually set the mode (D24's 'the layer that won'). internal/runstore's KnownRigorFrom is this set.

areas.description: Every area rule that matched, strictest first (D23), each with the mode it sets and the moment it was first applied at. Absent when none matched: a reader must not see 'there were rules' where the answer is 'there were none'. The order is one the record establishes wherever a block is built — the writer folds a moment in and sorts, the reader sorts a block the job may have written — so the first entry is the rule whose mode decided, which is what fugaro runs ls's MODE column names.

name.description: The rule's name, as its layer wrote it (internal/rigor's Area.Validate).

mode.description: The mode this rule sets (internal/rigor's vocabulary). It is carried per rule, not only on the block, because D23's order is by it: without it a reader could not check that the first entry is the strictest.

at.description: The moment of the run this rule was first applied at: the run's own moment it matched.
The moment of the resolution this block records: the last one that changed it, so a moment that resolved the same answer leaves it as it was.

revision.description: The revision of the configuration the mode was read from, origin/<base branch> (D25), so a run whose other keys came from the checked-out ref can be told apart from the mode it ran under (F35's 'two answers' made visible). Absent when the run could not name it.

tier.description: The expectation tier the run was dispatched at and what Fugaro expected a run of that tier to cost and take (docs/task-governance/implementation-plan.md T8.1, D330): fugaro run --tier, or the tier a --pr follow-up keeps from its PR, and the expectation the run's governance resolved for it (governance.tiers). Neither figure is a cap: the deployed per-run cap stays the ceiling whatever a tier expects (G6), so an expected cost above the cap is an expectation the run still stops at the cap for. Absent — never a block with an empty tier — for a run that carried no tier, which is every record written before this field existed, so an old reader sees the record it always saw and version stays 1 (the field is additive).
The tier (internal/tier's vocabulary). An unknown value is not a tier any runner resolved, and internal/runstore's TierRecord.Bounded refuses a block carrying one.

expected_usd.description: What a run of the tier is expected to cost, in dollars (policy.TierExpectation.ExpectedUSD). Bounded below and not above, like the same figure in fugaro.schema.json's governance.tiers: the project layer may loosen a tier past any figure Fugaro ships, and an expectation over the per-run cap is still only an expectation (G6), so a ceiling here would be a record the runner legally wrote that its own published schema calls impossible.

expected_minutes.description: What a run of the tier is expected to take, in minutes (policy.TierExpectation.ExpectedMinutes). Bounded below and not above, for the reason expected_usd is.

backlog.description: The ids of the backlog items this run filed for what it left open, in the order it filed them (docs/rigor-modes/implementation-plan.md T4.5, D9, D26). The item files are on the run's branch and in its pull request, where `fugaro backlog list` reads them. Nothing consumes this property yet — neither `fugaro diagnose` nor the console's run row carries the ids — and it is written anyway, because the record is what survives the run. Absent — never an empty list — for a run that filed none, which is every record written before this field existed, so an old reader sees the record it always saw.

items.description: One item id: the day the item was filed and the day's sequence, the name its file under docs/backlog/ opens with (internal/backlog's AllocateID).

tolerated.description: The findings the run's resolved mode let through, in the reviewer's own order (docs/rigor-modes/implementation-plan.md T3.4, D9, F19). The findings themselves and not only the count `reviews` carries, because what a mode decided not to fix is what a reader — and the backlog surface — needs. Bounded: at most 100 findings (runstore.MaxTolerated), each a score, two vocabulary values and a title of at most 200 runes. Absent — never an empty block — for a run that tolerated nothing, which is every record written before this field existed; the field is additive, so an old reader sees the record it always saw and `version` stays 1 (F21).

findings.description: One entry per tolerated finding, in the reviewer's order. Never empty: a run that tolerated nothing carries no block at all. Shorter than total only when the run tolerated more than 100 findings, which the cap makes a record of the first 100 rather than of the whole set.

title.description: The reviewer's own summary of the finding, clipped to 200 runes (runstore.MaxToleratedTitle) and redacted by the runner. It is the one piece of the finding's text the record carries; the whole summary stays in the transcript.

label.description: The word a person reads for the score (internal/rigor's label vocabulary). It is derived from the score and never an input to a decision (D2), so a reader takes the word from the axes beside it rather than trusting this one.

mode.description: The mode that tolerated the finding (internal/rigor's vocabulary): the run's resolved mode, which is one value (D22).

likelihood.description: How often the finding's condition will occur, on the anchored 1-5 scale (D1).

impact.description: How bad it is when it does (D1).

fix_cost.description: The effort to address it (D1). Only the modes whose sentence weighs it read it.

class.description: What kind of issue it is (D3, internal/rigor's vocabulary): the class is what the spec's severity override turned on.

total.description: How many findings the mode tolerated, so a record whose list was capped still says how many were let through. Never less than the length of findings.

review_scope.description: The comparison between the paths implement changed and the paths the review range covers, taken right after implement (docs/task-governance/implementation-plan.md T5.2, F2, D332). Report only: nothing halts on it, and it is the input of the digest's review-scope flag (T1.4) and of the review-scope stop (T7.3). Both sets are repository-relative paths git listed, read over the same range the review input is built from, so outside is exactly what the reviewer was handed that implement never wrote. Bounded (runstore.MaxReviewScopeFiles paths per list, the two lists together within runstore.MaxReviewScopeBytes of path, each path at runstore.MaxReviewScopePath runes). Absent for a run that died before the comparison, and in records from before this field existed; the field is additive, so `version` stays 1.

applicable.description: Whether the review range is the run's own commits — narrowed to them, or equal to them by construction — and so whether outside is a mismatch rather than a fact about a range kept wider on purpose. True exactly when why_not is absent. The two sets are read from one revision when it is true, so outside is empty by construction and a non-empty outside always comes with a why_not.

why_not.description: Why the comparison does not apply (internal/runstore's ReviewScope* values): a follow-up or a review run reviews the pull request's range; a report run's first step is the digest step, which no implement stage follows; an autofix gate skipped implement; a git older than 2.44 cannot say which commits are the run's own; the run made no commit of its own, or they could not be read; the recorded range holds no more commits than the run's own, so it was kept; the commit the run's own commits start after no longer leads to HEAD; or one of the comparison's own git reads failed. A reader renders this value and never task text.

implement_files.description: The paths the run's own commits changed, sorted as git listed them, at most 200 (runstore.MaxReviewScopeFiles). Absent — never an empty array — when there is no implement set to compare with, which why_not then says.

items.description: One repository-relative path, clipped to 512 runes (runstore.MaxReviewScopePath).

review_files.description: The paths the review range covers, the same way.

items.description: One repository-relative path, clipped to 512 runes.

outside.description: The paths in review_files that are not in implement_files: what the reviewer was handed that implement never wrote (F2). Absent when there are none.

items.description: One repository-relative path, clipped to 512 runes.

truncated.description: Set when one of the lists was capped at 200 paths, at 16 KiB of path between the two (runstore.MaxReviewScopeBytes), or one of its paths clipped at 512 runes: the stored sets are then not the whole ones.

backlog_closed.description: The ids of the backlog items this run closed as the follow-up whose review shipped the round an earlier run on its pull request left open (docs/rigor-modes D31, plan T4.7), in the order it closed them. The closed item files are on the run's branch, each with a `## Closed by` section naming the pull request. Nothing consumes this property yet. At most 64 (runstore.MaxBacklogClosed). Absent — never an empty list — for a run that closed none, which is every record written before this field existed.

items.description: One item id, as `backlog` writes them.

ab.description: The A/B pair block the run's task carried (docs/model-ab-testing, decisions D550-D573; runstore.Record.AB, task.AB): the pair both arms belong to, which arm this run is, and, for a challenger, the coder model it ran. It is the task's own block echoed onto the record, so a pair can be scored from records alone, without a bucket listing (D559). Absent — never a block with an empty arm — for a run that was not sampled, which is every record written before this field existed, so an old reader sees the record it always saw and version stays 1 (the field is additive). The enums are internal/task's own closed vocabulary, spelled exactly as it spells it, and they are the same ones task.schema.json carries: a task and the record it produces state one block the same way.

pair_id.description: The pair both arms belong to: one value, written by the launcher onto both tasks, so a reader joins the two records by it. Opaque to the runner, and a blank one names no pair (the pattern is task.Spec.Validate's strings.TrimSpace rule).

arm.description: Which arm this run is. The champion is the run the developer gets and publishes exactly as an unsampled run; the challenger is a shadow (task.ABArmChampion, task.ABArmChallenger).

publish.description: Present only on a challenger, and only as "none" (task.ABPublishNone): the challenger's arm never pushes, opens, updates or comments on a pull request (D554). A champion publishes as it always did and carries nothing here.

challenger.description: The coder model the challenger arm ran, and the one difference between the arms (D555). A blank one is no model (the pattern is task.Spec.Validate's strings.TrimSpace rule).

challenger_source.description: Who named the challenger: the owner, in the project layer, never the repository's own file (D556, task.ABChallengerOwner).

patch_object.description: The key of the run's own tree diff under the runs bucket, runs/<repo-slug>/<run-id>/ab/patch.diff: the diff from the run's StartSHA to its final head, with no commit metadata in it, which both arms upload because the paired comparison reads the two diffs. Absent for a run that uploaded none — every run before this field existed, and one that died before finalize — so an absent key means there is no patch, never that the patch is empty.

patch_truncated.description: Set when the stored patch is shorter than the run's real diff, because the object is capped: the truncation is recorded as a fact rather than hidden, as changed_files.truncated is, so a reader can tell a short patch from a cut-off one.
